senses.gloss: m. (preced.) fine, penalty, esp. the fine for seducing a girl (Deut. XXII, 29).
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 43a">Keth. 43ᵃ</cite> top, a. e. <he>מודה בק׳ פטור</he> he who confesses an act with which a fine is connected, is exempt from the fine; <cite ref="Ketubot 42a:5">ib. 42ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Shevuot 5:4">Shebu. V, 4</cite> <he>אינו משלם ק׳ על פי עצמו</he> none needs to pay a fine on his own confession (if he cannot be convicted otherwise). Keth. l. c. (in Chald. dict.) <he>ק׳ הוי</he> it is the case of a fine, opp. <cite ref="M01652"><he>ממונא</he></cite> the case of a real debt or indemnity. Ib. bot. <he>יצאו אלו שהן ק׳</he> exclude those cases which concern only a fine, opp. <cite ref="M01651"><he>ממון</he></cite>. Ib. III, 1 <he>יש להן ק׳</he> a fine is due for seducing them. Ib. 29ᵃ <he>יש לה מכר ואין לה ק׳</he> she can be sold (by her father), and no fine is due for her seduction. Ib. III, 8 <he>כל … מכר אין ק׳</he> wherever sale can take place, there is no fine for seduction. Ib. 3 <he>קְנָסָהּ לעצמה</he> the fine for her seduction belongs to herself (and not to her father); a. fr.—Pl. <he>קְנָסוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 8a:11">Snh. 8ᵃ</cite> <he>דיני ק׳ בכמה</he> how many judges are required for the adjudication of a fine? <cite ref="Ketubot 43a">Keth. 43ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—[<he>קנסות</he>, <cite ref="Zevachim 88b:2">Zeb. 88ᵇ</cite> ed., v. <cite ref="S00356"><he>קוֹלָס</he></cite>.]
